body:
A website's digital marketing strategy is built on two main pillars: organic traffic obtained through SEO optimization and paid traffic generated through Google Ads campaigns. Although often treated as two separate and even competing approaches, the two strategies complement each other and produce better results when used together in a coordinated way.

A common myth in digital marketing is that investing in Google Ads eliminates the need for SEO, or conversely, that good SEO makes paid advertising unnecessary. The reality is different: each channel addresses distinct business needs and has advantages the other cannot replicate. SEO builds lasting visibility over the long term, while Google Ads offers immediate results and precise control over targeting.

In this guide, you will discover how Google Ads works, which campaign types are available and how to use data from paid campaigns to improve your SEO strategy. You will also see how to allocate your budget efficiently between the two channels and which common mistakes to avoid to maximize every leu invested in digital marketing.

How Google Ads works and how it complements your SEO strategy


Google Ads and SEO operate on the same results page, but through different mechanisms. Understanding how they interact matters for an integrated digital marketing strategy that produces consistent, tangible results.

How Google Ads works


Google Ads is Google's advertising platform, which allows paid ads to be displayed in search results, on YouTube, in Gmail and on millions of partner websites. The predominant billing model is cost-per-click (CPC): you pay only when a user clicks your ad, not simply for displaying it.

The main types of Google Ads campaigns:

  • Search Ads: text ads displayed above and below the organic results on the Google search page
  • Shopping Ads: product ads that include an image, price and store name (for online stores)
  • Display Ads: banners displayed on websites in the Google Display Network
  • Video Ads: video ads on YouTube and in Google's video network
  • Performance Max: automated campaigns that display ads across all Google channels simultaneously
  • Demand Gen: campaigns for generating demand on YouTube, Discover and Gmail
Search Ads campaigns work through a real-time auction. When a user searches for a keyword you are targeting, Google evaluates your ad against competitors' ads based on two main factors: the bid (how much you are willing to pay per click) and Quality Score (the quality of the ad and landing page).

What Quality Score is and why it matters


Quality Score is a score from 1 to 10 that Google assigns to each keyword in a campaign. It reflects the ad's relevance to the user's query, the quality of the landing page and the expected click-through rate. A high Quality Score reduces cost per click and improves ad position, which is why SEO-optimized landing pages also provide a direct advantage in paid campaigns.

The formula for calculating ad position is simplified as follows:

Ad Rank = Suma licitată × Quality Score × Extensii și formate de anunț

An ad with a Quality Score of 8 and a bid of 1 leu can outperform a competing ad with a Quality Score of 4 and a bid of 2 lei. This means relevant landing page optimization reduces paid campaign costs.

How Google Ads and SEO complement each other


The relationship between the two channels goes deeper than simply coexisting on the same results page. Data and insights from each channel can improve the other's performance.

Dominating the search results page (SERP)


Appearing simultaneously with a paid ad and an organic result for the same search significantly increases the overall click-through rate. Studies show that appearing in both sections generates more clicks than appearing in just one, because users perceive the business as more credible and relevant.

This approach is particularly valuable for highly competitive searches, where SEO rules make it difficult to achieve the first organic position. The paid ad provides immediate visibility, while SEO efforts work to strengthen the organic position. When your ad is in the first paid position and your organic result is in the top 3, you occupy a considerable portion of the results page's visible space.

Google Ads data that improves SEO


Google Ads campaigns provide valuable data you can use to refine your SEO strategy:
  • Keywords that convert: the Search Terms report in Google Ads shows exactly which keywords generate conversions. Use these keywords in organic content to attract similar traffic without a cost per click
  • Testing titles: test different title and description variations in ads. Variations with a high CTR can be adapted for the meta titles and meta descriptions of organic pages
  • Discovering new keywords: the broad match option in Google Ads reveals searches you had not considered. Add them to your SEO strategy
  • Demographic data: Google Ads provides information about the age, gender and interests of people who convert. These data help you create targeted content for the right audience
  • Peak hours and days: scheduling reports in Ads show when users are most active and likely to convert: useful information for planning organic content publication

SEO data that improves Google Ads


The relationship also works in reverse. Data from Google Search Console provide valuable information for paid campaigns:
  • Keywords with high impressions but low CTR: if you appear organically but receive no clicks, these keywords may work better as paid ads with more appealing messages
  • Pages with good organic performance: use them as landing pages for Google Ads campaigns for a higher Quality Score
  • Seasonal trends: historical Search Console data show seasonal variations. Adjust your Google Ads budget to increase investment during peak periods
  • Search queries with commercial intent: identify organic terms with clear purchase intent and target them in Google Ads as well for maximum visibility

The correct structure for a Google Ads account


A well-organized Google Ads account structure makes campaign management and budget optimization easier. The standard hierarchy is:
  1. Account: the top level, associated with the email address and billing information
  2. Campaign: groups ads by objectives and budgets (e.g. "SEO services", "Web Design")
  3. Ad group: contains closely related thematic keywords and ads (e.g. "Local SEO", "E-commerce SEO")
  4. Ads: the actual text displayed to users
  5. Keywords: the terms you want your ads to appear for
A common mistake is grouping too many keywords in the same ad group. Ad groups with a specific theme have a higher Quality Score because the ad can be more relevant to each keyword in the group.

Keyword match types


Google Ads offers three keyword match types, each with specific advantages and disadvantages:
  • Broad match: the ad appears for broad variations of the keyword, including synonyms and related searches. Generates a lot of traffic, but may also include irrelevant searches
  • Phrase match: the ad appears for searches that include the exact phrase, with words before or after it. A good balance between volume and relevance
  • Exact match: the ad appears only for the exact search or very close variations. The most precise, but with lower volume
The practical recommendation is to start with phrase match and exact match to control costs, then experiment with broad match based on the data you have collected.

Budget allocation strategy between SEO and Google Ads


There is no universal formula for dividing your budget between SEO and Google Ads, but a few principles can guide your decision:
  • New businesses: invest more in Google Ads initially for immediate traffic, while building an organic presence through SEO. As organic visibility grows, gradually reduce the ads budget
  • Established businesses: balance the budget between the two channels. Use Google Ads for competitive keywords and SEO for long-tail keywords
  • Seasonal products: increase your Google Ads budget during peak periods and rely on SEO during quiet periods
  • Local services: combine local SEO with local Google Ads for maximum visibility in your area
A useful principle is the rule "SEO for steady traffic, Ads for peaks in demand". When you launch a new product or a limited-time promotion, Google Ads provides immediate visibility. SEO-optimized content works in the background to build authority and generate steady traffic over the long term.

Common mistakes when integrating Google Ads with SEO

  • Keyword cannibalization: running ads for keywords where you already rank 1 organically may waste your budget. Check whether adding the ad actually increases total traffic
  • Separate landing pages: sending paid traffic to different pages from organic traffic dilutes authority. When possible, use the same SEO-optimized pages as landing pages
  • Ignoring Quality Score: a low Quality Score increases cost per click. Pages with good Core Web Vitals and relevant content achieve a higher Quality Score
  • No conversion tracking: without conversion tracking, you cannot evaluate the effectiveness of either SEO or Google Ads. Configure Google Consent Mode v2 and track conversions from both sources
  • Daily budget too low: an insufficient budget causes ads to stop halfway through the day, generating incomplete data and poor performance
  • Not using ad extensions: extensions (sitelink, callout, phone call) increase ad visibility at no additional cost and improve CTR

Measuring combined results


To evaluate the effectiveness of your integrated strategy, monitor these metrics:
  • Total Share of Voice: the percentage of total impressions (organic + paid) you obtain vs. competitors
  • Blended cost per acquisition: the average cost per conversion calculated across both channels combined
  • Total search traffic: the sum of organic and paid traffic, monitored over time
  • Conversion rate per channel: compare conversion effectiveness for organic vs. paid traffic
  • ROAS (Return on Ad Spend): revenue generated per leu spent in Google Ads
Use monitoring tools to correlate traffic variations with changes in Google Ads campaigns and Google algorithm updates. When you notice a drop in organic traffic, Google Ads data can help you identify whether it is an SEO problem or a change in user behavior.

Connecting Google Ads with Google Analytics 4 allows you to see the entire user journey, from the ad click to conversion, and identify the pages that convert best. This information is useful both for optimizing paid campaigns and for your overall digital marketing strategy.

Google Ads and SEO are not competing strategies. They are complementary. Used together, they provide complete visibility in Google results, valuable data for ongoing optimization and the flexibility to adapt quickly to market changes. Start by analyzing existing data from both channels, identify opportunities for synergy and build an integrated strategy that maximizes every leu invested.
